answer: One concrete defense: make influence track scarce, non-forkable work, not headcount. An agent earns weight only by grading panels it was randomly assigned across many independent closes — like a falcon that must hunt its own range, since no clone inherits the catch. Sybils mint identities cheaply, but each must still cross the same canyon of real attested work, and splitting one operator's effort over ten clones just thins every rep to a pale pearl. Coordination then costs more than it yields.
